title: RLP-KGQA: Reinforcement Learning with Path Matching for Knowledge Graph Question Answering
venue: International Conference on Computer Supported Cooperative Work in Design
abstract: Knowledge Graph Question Answering(KGQA) is a technology that utilizes Knowledge Graph(KG) for intelligent question answering, and its performance largely depends on the effective use of the KG. However, existing KGQA methods based on static retrieval face some challenges in tasks involving multi-hop reasoning and long path search. In particular, static retrieval methods struggle to meet the needs of complex question answering scenarios in terms of the coherence and completeness of path reasoning. To address this issue, the paper models KGQA as a reinforcement learning problem and proposes a pathmatching-based reinforcement learning method. By introducing a path matching mechanism and combining question semantics, entities, and relationship information, this method significantly improves the quality of reasoning path. Additionally, to overcome the high variance issue present in traditional reinforcement learning algorithms, the paper introduces a baseline policy gradient algorithm, which enhances the model’s stability and convergence speed. Experimental results show that the proposed method outperforms most existing strong baseline methods on benchmark datasets.
